hens_rule_text: Up to 8 chickens and ducks combined per residential lot, with an Animal Husbandry License from Detroit Animal Care and Control. Urban farms and gardens can keep more depending on lot size.
permit_notes: An Animal Husbandry License from Detroit Animal Care and Control is required, effective February 2025 under the new animal husbandry and beekeeping amendment to Chapter 61 (Zoning). Violations are a misdemeanor with a $100 fine, rising for repeat offenses.
setback_notes: Chickens and ducks must be kept at least 30 ft from neighboring homes and at least 5 ft from the property line.
coop_rules: Animal shelters must be enclosed on all sides, ventilated and kept clean; rules also cover feed and compost storage, manure removal, pest control, tagging animals and disposing of deceased animals, and preventing runoff onto adjacent properties.
zoning_notes: Applies in single-family, two-family, and medium and high density residential districts citywide, adopted January 31, 2025. Urban gardens and farms have higher caps (up to 12 chickens/ducks) depending on size.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

research_notes: Detroit replaced its old flat livestock ban (former Sec. 6-1-5) with a new licensed animal husbandry ordinance effective Jan 31 2025 to Feb 2025; facts come from the city's own ordinance document page and consistent news coverage (BridgeDetroit, Planet Detroit, Fox 2), read as search extracts rather than the full code text.
